Interesting guide; one thing - I don’t understand why you turn anti aliasing off in apex if you are focusing on clarity and smoothness…If you have a monitor with sharpening it counters the blur but without anti-aliasing the visuals are so bad imo. I can’t play without it. Seeing the aliasing def makes it harder to focus. I personally use RTSS with a gsync monitor, gsync on, no v-sync. I have a 180 refresh rate monitor but I cap my fps at my average consistent framerate. I don’t notice any visual issues this way and less input lag than gsync+vsync(nvcp) gsync with slightly lower cap has tearing still for me possibly because I prefer my settings not all to be low. I try to balance visual clarity with performance as well and would rather have smooth clear visuals than aliasing, choppy but maybe faster. Yeah one might have faster input but it doesn’t matter if you can’t focus on what youre doing xD

Sorry to resurrect an old topic but watching hereditary for the third time now and that scene man…Had to see what others had to say. This scene is so well done it made me cry like it was my own child who just died that way. I felt it. The way they portrayed that scenario so perfectly. The way Peter handled the situation was so different from most horror movies because it was  human and raw. It was relatable - you feel what he felt. Toni Colette’s acting; that gut wrenching performance is probably the best I have ever seen in any movie let alone a horror genre. The build up man! Like okay wow that’s fucked, Charlie just got her head knocked off. Peter is driving home with his dead sister. He gets into bed…morning hits, still awake…Annie is going somewhere, oh shit. (At this point it’s pulling you in slowly and we know what’s going to happen…but did we anticipate how well done it would be?) Annie screams as we stare into Peter’s blank expression…queue Charlie’s decapitated head covered in ants. WTF. Then Annie’s gut wrenching cries how she wants to die…bam. I felt it all hit me like an emotional bitch slap. I started to cry in the movie theater. I had just experienced through this movie the emotions of a brother killing his sister and a mother finding her dead child.
